item: Row 427: a plaintext staged member is sealed at a 16 KiB page, read first when it fits, temp in memory
summary: seal_plaintext writes the sealed copy at a 16 KiB cipher page whatever the plaintext's page size (sqlcipher_export rebuilds anyway); reads the plaintext once front to back first, only when the file and a margin (512 MB or a quarter of the file) fit in the smaller of the machine's and the cgroup's available memory (no figure or an unreadable limit = no read; a failed read never fails the seal; OO_VALIDATE_WARM=0 turns it off); and sets temp_store = MEMORY before the export, so a build compiled otherwise can never spill plaintext sort runs to the OS temp folder (R842; an on-disk /proc/self/fd test with a control that catches an O_TMPFILE). Measured, 200k articles, 4 CPUs, cold: seal 111-123 s to 58-66 s at full memory; keyed walk beside the merge at 4 GB 106-109 s to 61-65 s. Re-measured on top of row 439 (100k articles): peak anonymous memory 825 MB at 16 KiB vs 846 MB at 4 KiB, merge 1-3 s faster; nothing added to the encrypted memory pre-check.
